name: Congenital Myasthenic Syndromes

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Consensus Diagnostic Criteria for Congenital Myasthenic Syndromes

criteria.description: Presence of fatigable muscle weakness from birth or early infancy
Abnormal neuromuscular transmission demonstrated by decremental response on repetitive nerve stimulation or single-fiber EMG
Identification of pathogenic variants in known CMS-associated genes
Improvement of symptoms with acetylcholinesterase inhibitors or other targeted therapies
Negative acetylcholine receptor and MuSK antibodies to exclude autoimmune myasthenia gravis

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of clinical fatigable weakness plus electrophysiological evidence of neuromuscular transmission defect and/or pathogenic genetic variant
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic confirmation is increasingly considered essential for definitive diagnosis.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Variable decremental response on repetitive nerve stimulation

common.symptomName: Bulbar muscle weakness causing dysphagia and dysarthria

laboratory: Negative acetylcholine receptor and MuSK antibodies
genetic: Pathogenic variants in genes such as CHRNE, RAPSN, COLQ, DOK7, and others
other: Electrophysiological evidence of neuromuscular transmission defect (repetitive nerve stimulation, single-fiber EMG)

distinguishingFeatures: Multisystem involvement including CNS and cardiac

redFlags: Lack of response to acetylcholinesterase inhibitors
references: Engel AG, Shen XM, Selcen D, Sine SM. What have we learned from the congenital myasthenic syndromes. J Mol Neurosci. 2010;40(1-2):143-153.

Abicht A, Dusl M, Gallenmüller C, et al. Congenital myasthenic syndromes: achievements and limitations of phenotype-guided gene-after-gene sequencing in diagnostic practice: a study of 680 patients. Hum Mutat. 2012;33(4):561-572.
Rodriguez Cruz PM, Palace J, Beeson D. Congenital myasthenic syndromes. Ann N Y Acad Sci. 2018;1412(1):104-113.
